proposals.reason: The enclosing switch reaches this expression only for M, m, C, or c, so case-folding the same unchanged format byte always produces M or C.
proposals.evidence: The switch expression and both comparisons read pszCurrentFormat[anCurrentFormatOffset[nPosition]] without an intervening mutation. For M/m the first comparison is false; for C/c the first is true and the second is false.

proposals.reason: The cooperative loop returns earlier whenever Timeout is zero, before control can reach this repeated zero-timeout test.
proposals.evidence: Timeout is passed by value and is not modified between the dominating return at lines 375-376 and this else-if.

proposals.reason: The initialized flag becomes true only after the final fallible initialization operation has succeeded, and the function then commits success before entering cleanup.
proposals.evidence: Every failure before ODMutexInitialize succeeds reaches cleanup with bQueueMutexInitialized false. After it succeeds, the flag is set, only non-failing field assignments and ODInQueueResetLastActivity remain, and Result is set to kODRCSuccess so cleanup is skipped.

proposals.reason: In a non-threaded build, no operation can fail after the event array has been allocated.
proposals.evidence: The event allocation is the final fallible operation when OD_MULTITHREADED is absent. A null event pointer reaches cleanup, while a non-null event pointer proceeds through non-failing assignments, resets activity, sets Result to success, and skips cleanup.

proposals.reason: The immediately preceding zero-character branch exits the input loop, so the second condition is always true whenever this compound decision is reached.
proposals.evidence: Line 362 tests LastInputEvent.chKeyPress == 0 and breaks at line 364. No assignment to chKeyPress occurs before line 368; therefore the nonzero term cannot independently change this decision's result, although both decision outcomes remain reachable through bFromRemote.

proposals.reason: Every path reaching the final fallback has a nonempty sequence buffer.
proposals.evidence: An empty buffer either obtains a nonzero character, which populates it, or enters doorway mode, whose completion and failure paths return earlier. Pending doorway promotion with an empty buffer also enters the earlier-returning doorway path. Existing nonempty input remains nonempty because each preceding shift is immediately followed by return.

proposals.reason: Normal loop termination after recognizing a color control always leaves at least one ordinary character in the final display segment.
proposals.evidence: Reaching this else-if requires bNotFound to be false, so a color control was recognized. Each recognized control either exits early when no following display character exists or resets nCharCount to zero with pchCurrent pointing at a non-null following character. A subsequent control repeats that rule. The loop can therefore terminate normally only after its ordinary-character arm increments nCharCount at least once after the final recognized control.

proposals.reason: The local menu pointer is initialized to NULL and cannot be changed before this test.
proposals.evidence: paMenuItems is initialized to NULL in its declaration at function entry. The only preceding statements initialize OpenDoors, enter the API, normalize box characters, validate the level, copy scalar arguments, and reject a null text pointer; none assigns paMenuItems.

proposals.reason: A nonzero pending item count cannot coexist with a full menu when the parsing loop exits.
proposals.evidence: btCurrentNumMenuItems increases only in the pipe arm, which resets btCount to zero. Once the count reaches MAX_MENU_ITEMS, the loop exits before another character can make btCount nonzero. If the loop instead ends at the string terminator with btCount nonzero, the count remains below the limit.

proposals.reason: The line boundary cannot stop rendering while an unrendered menu item remains.
proposals.evidence: btBottom is assigned btTop + btCurrentNumMenuItems + 1, btLineCount starts at btTop + 1, and both btCount and btLineCount advance exactly once per completed iteration. Therefore btCount < btCurrentNumMenuItems implies btLineCount < btBottom.

proposals.reason: Every path to session_ended has already acquired arrow-key ownership.
proposals.evidence: All jumps to session_ended occur in the input loop below the unconditional ODStatStartArrowUse call and grabbedArrow = TRUE assignment. No statement clears grabbedArrow before cleanup.

proposals.reason: The preceding destroy condition can fall through only when MENU_KEEP is set and the command is positive.
proposals.evidence: The preceding if is (!(wCurrentFlags & MENU_KEEP)) || nCommand <= 0. Reaching this else-if proves both operands false, which necessarily makes wCurrentFlags & MENU_KEEP true.

proposals.reason: A filename accepted by the preceding bounded token extraction cannot fill the larger resolved-path buffer.
proposals.evidence: szFilename contains 80 bytes including its terminator, and ODListGetFirstWord returns false unless the complete token fits. Therefore strlen(szFilename) is at most 79, while szResolvedPath contains 100 bytes and this test requires a length of at least 100.

proposals.reason: The backward scan is entered only after strchr has established that the filename contains a directory separator or drive colon, and it breaks when that known delimiter is reached.
proposals.evidence: The filename is not mutated between the strchr tests at lines 138-139 and the scan. wCurrent begins at strlen(filename), remains positive until the scan examines the established delimiter, and that iteration exits through break rather than the loop condition.

proposals.reason: The switch expression is the index of a loop bounded to the 49 explicitly handled configuration keywords.
proposals.evidence: The switch is reached only when strcmp matches od_config_text[wCurrent] inside for(wCurrent = 0; wCurrent < TEXT_SIZE; ++wCurrent). TEXT_SIZE is 49 and the switch contains cases 0 through 48, so its implicit default cannot be selected.

proposals.reason: Masking the interrupt-identification register with 0x06 permits only the four values explicitly handled by the switch.
proposals.evidence: For every byte value, btIIR & 0x06 is exactly 0x00, 0x02, 0x04, or 0x06. All four values have case labels, so the implicit default cannot be selected.

proposals.reason: A 16-bit INT cannot supply dimensions whose product exceeds the largest cell count accepted by this test.
proposals.evidence: Both dimensions are INT values after minimum selection. Their largest positive 16-bit values are 32767, whose product is 1073676289, below 0xffffffff / 2. Nonpositive values return at the preceding dimension check.

proposals.reason: Every supported platform either has a size_t capable of representing the accepted byte count or rejects a larger DOS object before this conversion.
proposals.evidence: Modern, Windows, and DOS32 builds use a size_t at least as wide as unsigned long. DOS16 rejects ulBytes greater than 65486 immediately above, and every remaining value fits its 16-bit unsigned size_t. The narrowing round trip therefore cannot differ.

proposals.reason: A validated cursor row always terminates the plain-text replay loop before its condition can become false.
proposals.evidence: Validation requires dwCursorRow from 1 through dwBottom - dwTop + 1, which is no greater than nCurrentHeight. The loop starts at row 1 and breaks unconditionally when nRow equals dwCursorRow, so every reachable iteration sequence exits through that break rather than the loop condition's false outcome.

proposals.reason: Buffered display cannot write a later character above the first invalidated row.
proposals.evidence: The first printable character initializes btTopMost to the current row, while a scroll initializes it to the window top. Within the call, line feed, tab wrapping, and printable wrapping can only retain or increase the cursor row; carriage return and backspace do not change it. No later btRow can therefore be less than btTopMost.

proposals.reason: The memory-backed Unix and Windows initialization paths cannot make bClear false.
proposals.evidence: bClear is initialized to TRUE. On Unix and Windows, the only compiled platform blocks allocate a memory screen and do not assign bClear before this decision; assignments to FALSE exist only in the excluded DOS video-mode blocks.

proposals.reason: Every path that makes bEOF true returns before the while condition can be evaluated again.
proposals.evidence: A final stat failure returns kODRCEndOfFile, an accepted final entry returns kODRCSuccess, and a rejected final entry returns kODRCEndOfFile. Non-final skipped or rejected entries continue only while bEOF remains false. The earlier bEOF check returns before the loop when it is already true.

proposals.reason: On 32-bit Windows, size_t and UINT have the same maximum value, so a size_t result cannot exceed (UINT)-1.
proposals.evidence: The first condition independently covers ODSizeAdd failure and success. On Windows x86, successful ODSizeAdd stores into a 32-bit size_t, making the second condition nGrownSize > UINT_MAX invariantly false. Windows x64 separately exercises that condition both true and false.

proposals.reason: On 32-bit Windows, size_t and UINT have the same maximum value, so a size_t result cannot exceed (UINT)-1.
proposals.evidence: ODSizeAdd failure and success are independently exercised. A successful ODSizeAdd result greater than UINT_MAX cannot be represented by Windows x86 size_t; Windows x64 separately exercises the greater-than condition both true and false.

proposals.reason: On 32-bit Windows, size_t and UINT have the same maximum value, so a size_t result cannot exceed (UINT)-1.
proposals.evidence: ODSizeAdd failure and success are independently exercised. A successful ODSizeAdd result greater than UINT_MAX cannot be represented by Windows x86 size_t; Windows x64 separately exercises the greater-than condition both true and false.

proposals.reason: Every scan that finds a first difference also finds a finish position before it can leave the current line.
proposals.evidence: After bFoundStart becomes true, equal characters set bFoundFinish directly; otherwise either line ending sets it before the loop's end-of-line break. With neither ending present, the scan continues. A later difference can clear the flag, but the same invariant reestablishes it before that line ends.

proposals.reason: The line-array capacity advances from zero only in exact LINE_ARRAY_GROW_SIZE increments, so exercising this guard requires constructing and indexing nearly UINT_MAX lines.
proposals.evidence: unProcessingLine starts at zero and growth occurs only when it equals unLineArraySize; each successful growth adds 20. Modern UINT widths require billions of indexed lines. With 16-bit UINT, the pointer array reaches the 16-bit size_t allocation limit well before the 65,520-line capacity that would make this guard true.

proposals.reason: The editor's character-advance loop evaluates IS_EOL_CHAR(*pch) only while *pch is non-NUL.
proposals.evidence: The enclosing for condition requires *pch to be non-NUL. Therefore the NUL comparison in the macro expansion at the loop body's first statement is invariantly false, while LF, CR, and ordinary-character outcomes are all exercised.

proposals.reason: The expanded IS_EOL_CHAR predicate includes pch[1] == NUL, while the enclosing conjunction requires pch[1] != NUL.
proposals.evidence: LF, CR, NUL, non-EOL, same-EOL, and different-EOL next bytes are exercised. The NUL arm of IS_EOL_CHAR and the following non-NUL test cannot independently cause the whole conjunction to be true, so LLVM's expanded five-condition MC/DC model is unsatisfiable; the portable three-condition source model is complete.

proposals.reason: Reaching the final data-bit comparison proves that the two-bit mask has value DATABITS_EIGHT.
proposals.evidence: DATABITS_MASK contains exactly two bits and the preceding comparisons exclude values zero, one, and two. The only remaining masked value is three, which is DATABITS_EIGHT, so this final condition cannot be false when evaluated.

proposals.reason: STOP_ONE_POINT_FIVE and STOP_TWO are the same encoded bit value, and STOP_MASK has only that one bit.
proposals.evidence: After STOP_ONE is false, the masked value must be 0x04, so the STOP_ONE_POINT_FIVE comparison is invariantly true. Its branch therefore consumes every value that could reach the identical STOP_TWO comparison, making the latter unreachable.

proposals.reason: The 16-bit Watcom FOSSIL retry is expressed as a do-while loop whose condition is the constant TRUE.
proposals.evidence: The test exercises both a failed FOSSIL send that repeats the body and a successful send that exits through the body break. Because the loop condition is the constant TRUE, its false edge cannot occur.

proposals.reason: A single-threaded isolated test cannot both enter the empty UART wait with a null idle callback and later make the queue nonempty so the function returns.
proposals.evidence: The callback-present path is exercised with the callback supplying the byte, and the callback-null configuration is exercised when a byte is already queued. Entering the loop with both an empty queue and no callback has no operation capable of changing nRXChars and therefore cannot terminate without an external interrupt producer.

proposals.reason: The cleanup test and unsupported return follow an unconditional break in the Door32 switch arm.
proposals.evidence: Both successful and failed Door32 writes are exercised with converted and original buffers. A successful write executes break at line 3794, while a failed write returns at line 3792, so neither path can reach lines 3795-3796.

proposals.reason: A single-threaded isolated test cannot fill the UART queue, enter the remaining-data path with a null idle callback, and subsequently free queue space so the function terminates.
proposals.evidence: The callback-present path is exercised with a callback that drains the queue, and callback-null operation is exercised when the complete buffer fits in the queue. With remaining data, a full queue, and no callback or external UART interrupt producer, the loop has no operation that can create space.

proposals.reason: The DOS implementation rejects every mode except P_WAIT before reaching the two later mode tests.
proposals.evidence: The invalid-mode case exercises the return at lines 331-336. Every path continuing beyond it has nModeFlag equal to P_WAIT, making the test at line 389 always true and the repeated not-P_WAIT test at line 442 always false. The P_WAIT bodies and the earlier rejection are both exercised.

proposals.reason: No failure operation follows successful creation of the up-down control.
proposals.evidence: Every failure before line 381 leaves hwndTimeUpDown null. Once CreateWindowEx returns a non-null up-down handle, the remaining operations are unchecked setters, bSuccess is set true, and cleanup is skipped. All reachable creation-failure stages and the successful path are exercised.

proposals.reason: The unthreaded socket wait is expressed as a while loop whose condition is the constant 1.
proposals.evidence: The tests exercise a would-block result that continues, a one-byte result that iterates, and EOF and non-would-block errors that leave through the body break. The loop condition itself cannot evaluate false.

proposals.reason: Bitwise OR with the nonzero EV_RLSD constant makes this condition invariantly true.
proposals.evidence: The tests exercise unrelated and carrier-loss event masks and both carrier states. No DWORD event mask can make dwEvtMask | EV_RLSD equal zero; TODO.md tracks replacing the union with the intended mask test.

proposals.reason: Reaching the final identifier comparison proves that the identifier is 11.
proposals.evidence: The loop bounds btIdentifier to 0 through 11. The preceding arms exclude values 0 through 9 and then 10, leaving only 11 when this else-if is evaluated. BRIGHT, FLASHING, and all color identifiers are exercised.

proposals.reason: The parameter-count term is necessarily true when the final ANSI J arm is reached.
proposals.evidence: The preceding arm excludes btNumParams == 0 and parameter zero. Since btNumParams is unsigned, reaching this expression proves btNumParams >= 1; parameter values one and other positive values exercise both decision outcomes.

proposals.reason: The parameter-count term is necessarily true when the second ANSI K arm is reached.
proposals.evidence: The preceding arm excludes btNumParams == 0 and parameter zero. The unsigned count must therefore be at least one; parameter one and other positive values exercise both decision outcomes.

proposals.reason: The parameter-count term is necessarily true when the third ANSI K arm is reached.
proposals.evidence: The first ANSI K arm excludes count zero and parameter zero, and the second arm excludes parameter one. Thus the unsigned count is at least one whenever this expression is evaluated; parameter two and other positive values exercise both outcomes.

proposals.reason: The local-file section-found term is true on every path reaching this else-if.
proposals.evidence: The immediately preceding else-if consumes every path where bSectionFound is false. Both matching and nonmatching following section lines exercise the strncmp term, but bSectionFound cannot independently be false here.

proposals.reason: The remote-file section-found term is true on every path reaching this else-if.
proposals.evidence: The immediately preceding else-if continues whenever bSectionFound is false. Matching and nonmatching following section lines exercise the strncmp term, while bSectionFound cannot independently be false at this expression.

proposals.reason: The local bNormal flag is always true.
proposals.evidence: bNormal is initialized to TRUE at line 123 and has no other assignment or address escape before this test. The jump is therefore always taken; TODO.md records simplifying the invariant dispatch after its current behavior is retained by tests.

proposals.reason: The current-attribute-is-unknown term is false on every path reaching this decision.
proposals.evidence: The enclosing else is reached only when od_cur_attrib is not -1 and full-color output is disabled. The intervening reset path assigns -1 and jumps above this decision. Tests vary the brightness comparison and exercise both decision outcomes, but the repeated unknown-attribute term cannot independently become true; TODO.md records its removal after preserving the behavioral baseline.

proposals.reason: Each Boolean state is repeated in both arms of an expanded inequality, so the four syntactic conditions cannot vary independently.
proposals.evidence: The test drives all four combinations of od_last_input and bSysopColor and observes both decision outcomes and both color transitions. Each occurrence of either state is necessarily correlated with its negated occurrence, preventing source-level MC/DC for the four separately instrumented conditions. TODO.md records expressing the same established behavior as a Boolean inequality.

proposals.reason: The token-length counter cannot exceed 32, so this comparison is always true.
proposals.evidence: The parser increments wCurrent only inside if(wCurrent < 32); after it reaches 32, the remaining token bytes advance only pchConfigText. Empty, short, exactly 32-character, and overlong tokens exercise the established termination and truncation behavior, but cannot reach the else branch. TODO.md records removing the unreachable overflow handling.

proposals.reason: The keyword loop always leaves wCurrent equal to TEXT_SIZE before this decision.
proposals.evidence: A built-in match enters a switch but does not break the enclosing for loop; unmatched input also runs the loop to completion. Tests exercise built-in and unknown lines with both null and non-null callbacks, covering both decision outcomes while wCurrent >= TEXT_SIZE cannot independently be false. TODO.md records retaining the established all-lines callback contract while removing this invariant term.

proposals.reason: On the pthread path, the earlier initialization check dominates this repeated bODInitialized term.
proposals.evidence: The function returns at lines 1307-1311 when bODInitialized is false. In the pthread configuration, no function call or assignment between that guard and this decision can clear bODInitialized. Tests independently vary the pending-update, deferred-shutdown, and time-update-result terms and exercise both decision outcomes.
